name: The Tea Room at Wah
signature_dish: Kangra thali with first-flush Kangra tea
why_it_matters: The cafe arm of Wah Tea Estate (founded 1857; bought by the Prakash family in 1953) — set inside a working 526-acre tea garden with the Dhauladhars in the window. The Kangra thali is the most credible dham you'll get in a sit-down setting near Palampur.
insider_tip: Closed Tuesdays. Call ahead on +91 60052 31597 if you're a group of four or more — kitchen cooks to order, walk-in waits run 30+ minutes on weekends.
signature_address: Wah Tea Estate, Tehsil Palampur, VPO Patti, Palampur 176061

name: Takri — Natives' Kitchen & Cafe
why_it_matters: A 324-sqm Binary Studio-designed pavilion on the Dharamshala-Palampur road, opposite Gopalpur Tea Estate. Built specifically to serve Kangri dham at lunch — leaf plates, raised platforms, Nati performances on busier evenings — without the pretence of a wedding hall.
insider_tip: Dham is a lunch dish here, not all-day. Aim for the 12-3pm window; the wood-fired pizzas are the dependable evening order if you arrive late.
signature_address: Dharamshala-Palampur Road, near Gopalpur Tea Estate, Palampur 176081

name: Cloud 7
signature_dish: Dhaba chicken curry on the rotating top deck
why_it_matters: The 7th-floor revolving restaurant inside RS Sarovar Portico — Palampur's only one. A full rotation takes about an hour, putting the Dhauladhars in every seat. Buffet-led; the kitchen leans on home-style Indian rather than the hotel-bar continental cliché.
insider_tip: Book a window booth between 5-7pm — sunset hits the snow line and you'll catch it twice on the rotation. Walk-ins on weekends are turned away by 8pm.
signature_address: RS Sarovar Portico, Palampur-Dharamshala Road, Ghuggar, Palampur 176061

name: Coy's Cafe
why_it_matters: Specialty-coffee-focused cafe attached to Hotel Fresco on Lohna Road — currently #2 of 36 on TripAdvisor Palampur. Roasts and pulls espresso properly, which is rare in the Kangra Valley outside the Bir bubble.
insider_tip: Order coffee à la carte, not from the breakfast set — the set drinks default to instant. Ask for the single-origin pour at the counter.
signature_address: Hotel Fresco, Lohna Road, Bundla, Palampur 176061

name: Cliffy's Cafe
why_it_matters: Eco-cafe in Bundla village, just off Lohna Road — bakes in-house, runs a credible south-Indian breakfast (rare this far north), and the pizzas come out of a real oven. The everyday cafe locals default to when Coy's is full.
insider_tip: It's set 2nd-floor at KBL Plaza, easy to miss from the road. The terrace seats with the Dhauladhar view are unmarked — ask the staff.
signature_address: 2nd Floor, KBL Plaza, Lohna Road, Bundla, Palampur 176061

name: Off-Road Cafe & Pizzeria
why_it_matters: Run by Himalayan Adrenaline (Great Himalayan Adventure Studio) inside Raipur Tea Estate — pizzeria + ATV + paintball combined. Easy stop on the Bundla side; serves a passable Kangri dham alongside the wood-fired pies.
insider_tip: Bundle the pizza lunch with the on-site ATV ride if you're travelling with teens; both are billed through the same Himalayan Adrenaline desk.

name: Nitya Cafe
signature_dish: Maggi and chai at the Neugal river
why_it_matters: A tiny river-side cafe near the Saurabh Van Vihar / Om project — reached only on foot via a bamboo bridge over the Neugal. Worth it for the setting more than the menu; a clean halt on the Saurabh Van walk.
insider_tip: Bring an ID — there's a hydro-project checkpoint on the way in. No vehicles past the gate; the walk is ~500m and slippery in monsoon.

name: Verma Dhaba
why_it_matters: The mutton dhaba locals queue for, on the Mandi-Pathankot highway through Maranda. Unlimited pahadi mutton-rice plate goes for under ₹250; the kind of place where the bench fills before noon and clears by 2pm.
insider_tip: Cash only and seating is 15-20 covers — go before 1pm or accept a wait. Mutton runs out by mid-afternoon on Sundays.
signature_address: Mandi-Pathankot Road (NH-154), Maranda, Bag Uparla, Palampur 176102

name: The Tea Bud Restaurant (HPTDC)
why_it_matters: The state-tourism (HPTDC) hotel restaurant, tea-garden-side at the top of town. Honest hill-station kitchen — Indian, Chinese, continental — with a garden for tea on a sunny afternoon. The default no-surprise lunch when nothing else is open.
insider_tip: Government tariff means alcohol is licensed and ID-checked; the bar is the only one in town with a published menu. Dial +91 1894 231298 to confirm dinner hours off-season.

name: Araiya Palampur — The Dining Room
why_it_matters: The all-day dining room of Araiya — a 25-room luxury resort at 5,000ft on Bundla Tea Estate Road. Kangri menu is taken seriously; rooftop bar with a Dhauladhar wall is the best post-dinner seat in Palampur.
insider_tip: Walk-ins for non-residents are allowed but call first — the kitchen blocks for in-house weddings on weekends. Sunday brunch is the value pick.
